analysis.title: US Equity Strategy 3Q26 Earnings Brief: November 18
key_insights: NVDA reported 3Q beat: EPS $2.68 vs $2.48 consensus, revenue $115.8bn (+103% y/y) vs $109.1bn consensus, data center revenue $107.6bn vs $101.9bn consensus.
NVDA gross margin was 74.9%, about 90bp above the 74.0% estimate. Q4 gross margin guided at 71%-72%, broadly in line with expectations.
NVDA guided Q4 revenue to $126.1-$133.9bn vs $125.25bn consensus. FY2028 revenue growth outlook raised to about 75% y/y from 70%, off a higher FY2027 base.
91.7% of the S&P 500's market cap has reported. 3Q expectations are revenue growth of 14.8% and EPS growth of 32.8%. A later figure in the report puts expected 3Q EPS growth at 33.0% y/y.
Earnings are beating estimates by 5.8% on aggregate, with 77% of companies topping projections. EPS is on pace for 33.0% growth if the historical pattern of revisions holds.

Expected 3Q EPS growth by group: TECH+ 50.7%, Financials 11.0%, Non-Cyclicals 10.7%, Cyclicals ex-Energy 20.3%, Energy 155.2%. Only Energy, Materials and TECH+ are expected to outpace the S&P 500, and REITs are a drag.
The six largest TECH+ companies are expected to grow EPS 25.6% vs 35.2% for the rest of the market.
EPS and revenue beats are being rewarded less than in prior quarters. The threshold for a positive price reaction is slightly higher.
3Q26 EPS revisions improved over the last 3 months. Estimates normally fall into reporting season and recover as results come in, which did not happen this quarter.
2026E S&P 500 EPS is expected to grow 29.6% on consensus estimates.
In the next 5 trading days, 23 companies representing 3.3% of S&P 500 market cap report, including Walmart, Intuit, Ross Stores, Hewlett Packard, Agilent and Dell.

market_movers.rationale: The report summarizes NVDA's 3Q beat and raised FY2028 growth outlook. The rating is from the disclosure table, not a new call.

earnings_insights: NVDA 3Q reported: EPS $2.68 vs $2.48 consensus est, revenue $115.8bn (+103% y/y) vs $109.1bn consensus est, data center revenue $107.6bn vs $101.9bn consensus est.
NVDA Q4 guidance: revenue $126.1-$133.9bn vs $125.25bn consensus est, gross margin 71%-72% broadly in line with expectations.
Big 6 TECH+ 3Q26 EPS growth y/y, expected vs actual: META -6.9% vs 3.8%, GOOGL 6.3% vs -5.8%, MSFT 14.4% vs 18.3%, AMZN 2.0% vs -2.0%, AAPL 5.5% vs 9.0%, NVDA 88.9% vs 104.5%.
S&P 500 3Q26 aggregate EPS surprise is +5.8% with 77% of companies beating. Surprise thresholds are +/-1% for earnings and +/-0.25% for revenue.

UBS adjustments to reported EPS: META adjusted EPS $7.40 excluding a $9.89bn litigation charge, GOOG reported $2.12 including $8.7bn unrealised equity losses, BAC reported $0.91 including a $1.2bn AML settlement charge, JPM reported $5.57 including $658mn investment securities losses, ELV adjusted lower for a $1.85 per share non-operating benefit, AAPL diluted EPS $2.10 includes $0.05 from tariff refunds, CHTR excludes a $6.3bn franchise impairment.
LLY reported EPS $7.48 after $4.2bn IPR&D charges and MRK reported EPS $2.49 after $400mn IPR&D charges. UBS made no adjustments to these.
risk_factors: Beats are being rewarded less, so the bar for a positive price reaction has risen.
Aggregate S&P 500 EPS growth leans heavily on TECH+, which has had an outsized impact on growth over the past year.
The report cites macro variables, economic slowdown, a weaker currency and government policy changes as general risks.
